name: Microwave Butter Popcorn (High-Risk Pericarp Hull Warning)
whyItWorks: The #1 universally recognized food hazard in Crohn's and Colitis. The popped white starch is harmless, but every kernel retains a razor-sharp, concave brown pericarp hull made of indestructible insoluble cellulose. These hulls adhere to mucosal ulcers and form phytobezoar plugs in strictures.
prepOrOrderInstructions: Absolute Warning: Completely avoid popcorn in all forms (microwave, cinema, bagged, kettle corn). If craving a crunchy puffed snack, eat puffed Chester's Puffcorn (which is 100% hull-free) or pirate's booty puffs.
watchOuts: Highest-risk food for small bowel impaction and severe bleeding in IBD. Hulls lodge in intestinal ulcerations and do not digest.
